title: CVE-2021-22945: UAF and double-free in MQTT sending
excerpt:
# Vulnerability Description
libcurl version 7.77.0 has a [Use-After-Free](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-7_77_0/lib/mqtt.c#L559) and a [Double-Free](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-7_77_0/lib/mqtt.c#L560) in `lib/mqtt.c` in the function `mqtt_doing` on [lines 556 - 563](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-7_77_0/lib/mqtt.c#L556):
```c
if(mq->nsend) {
  /* send the remainder of an outgoing packet */
  char *ptr = mq->sendleftovers;
  result = mqtt_send(data, mq->sendleftovers, mq->nsend);
  free(ptr);
  if(result)
    return result;
}
```
As can be seen in the code above `mq->sendleftovers` gets freed in line 560 but not set to `NULL`. If `mqtt_doing` gets called repeatedly and the values of `mq->nsend` and `mq->sendleftovers` don't change this can result in
1. Sending the metadata of the freed chunk over the network via `mqtt_send`
2. Freeing `mq->sendleftovers` multiple times

`mq->nsend` and `mq->sendleftovers` get set in the function `mqtt_send` if `Curl_write` cannot send all bytes in the write-buffer at once. This can e.g. happen if `write()` returns `EAGAIN` or `EWOULDBLOCK`. Then `Curl_write` sets the number of written bytes to `0` and returns `CURLE_OK`.     
This can trigger the vulnerabilities as follows:
1. Supply an `mqtt://` URL to curl
2. Have some successfull transmissions with `mqtt_send`
3. At some point have an unsuccessfull transmission such that not all bytes of the write-buffer can be sent.
This causes `mq->sendleftovers` and `mq->nsend` to be set.
4. Have another invocation of `mqtt_doing`. The code mentioned above gets executed. `mq->sendleftovers` gets freed.
If `mqtt_send` could send all remaining bytes successfully `mq->sendleftovers` and `mq->nsend` don't get reset.
5. Have another invocation of `mqtt_doing`. Since `mq->nsend` didn't change curl tries to send the leftover bytes again, triggering the vulnerabilities

# How to reproduce the bug
1. Checkout tag `curl-7_77_0` in the curl repository
2. Apply the following patch that artificially creates a scenario as described above:
```
diff --git a/lib/sendf.c b/lib/sendf.c
index e41bb805f..773d4b5b6 100644
--- a/lib/sendf.c
+++ b/lib/sendf.c
@@ -294,6 +294,7 @@ void Curl_failf(struct Curl_easy *data, const char *fmt, ...)
  * If the write would block (CURLE_AGAIN), we return CURLE_OK and
  * (*written == 0). Otherwise we return regular CURLcode value.
  */
+static i

summary: Use-After-Free and double-free in libcurl's MQTT client when handling partial writes.

claims.text: mq->sendleftovers is freed without being set to NULL, leading to use-after-free if mqtt_doing is called again
claims.reasoning: The code at lines 556-563 frees mq->sendleftovers via ptr but never nulls out mq->sendleftovers or resets mq->nsend. On a subsequent call to mqtt_doing with unchanged mq->nsend, the dangling pointer is passed to mqtt_send (use-after-free) and freed again (double-free).

citations.note: free(ptr) called without setting mq->sendleftovers = NULL
condition checks mq->nsend, not whether pointer is valid

claims.text: mq->nsend and mq->sendleftovers are set in mqtt_send when Curl_write cannot send all bytes, but they are not reset after successful send
claims.reasoning: mqtt_send sets mq->nsend and mq->sendleftovers only on partial writes (len != n). On a subsequent full write, mqtt_send does not modify these fields, but mqtt_doing frees the buffer without clearing them, leaving stale values for the next iteration.

citations.note: nsend calculated as len - n when partial write occurs
sendleftovers allocated via Curl_memdup for unsent portion
free(ptr) in mqtt_doing without resetting mq->nsend or mq->sendleftovers

claims.text: When Curl_write returns 0 due to blocking, the code may trigger the double-free path on subsequent calls
claims.reasoning: Curl_write returns CURLE_OK with *written=0 when the socket would block (CURLE_AGAIN path). This makes mqtt_send see n=0, so len != n is true for any non-zero len, causing it to allocate leftovers for the entire buffer and set mq->nsend. The subsequent mqtt_doing call frees that buffer but leaves mq->nsend non-zero, enabling the double-free on the next call.

citations.note: Curl_write called, n receives bytes written
if(len != (size_t)n) triggers leftover logic when n=0

key_reasons: The code in lib/mqtt.c lines 556-563 frees mq->sendleftovers without setting it to NULL or resetting mq->nsend.
mqtt_send (lines 112-132) sets mq->sendleftovers and mq->nsend only on partial writes; on a later full write it leaves them unchanged.
Curl_write can return 0 bytes written with CURLE_OK (lines 332-335 in lib/sendf.c), which triggers the partial-write path in mqtt_send.

This creates a reachable use-after-free and double-free when the network socket blocks temporarily (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK), a realistic condition an attacker can influence by not reading data fast enough.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and reproduction steps. The code confirms the use-after-free and double-free in mqtt_doing: mq->sendleftovers is freed at line 560 without being nulled, and mq->nsend is not reset. When Curl_write returns 0 due to blocking (CURLE_AGAIN path in lib/sendf.c:332-335), mqtt_send sets the leftovers for the full buffer; a subsequent successful send frees the buffer but leaves the stale pointer and length, causing the double-free on the next mqtt_doing call. This is a valid security issue. We will prepare a fix that clears mq->sendleftovers and mq->nsend after freeing.
